The key mediator is therefore the miR-181b-1–AGO/RISC complex acting on the CYLD 3′UTR, not STAT3 occupancy, so the direction inverts — loss of the microRNA raises CYLD. Functionally, the resulting excess CYLD (a K63-deubiquitinating enzyme) strips ubiquitin chains from NEMO/TRAF and dampens IKK/NF-κB signaling, which in turn feeds back to lower STAT3-driven miR-181b-1, closing the loop.

Note that this is a derepression, not an induction of PTEN transcription — the change in PTEN output is attributable to loss of microRNA-mediated repression rather than to new PTEN promoter activity.
